Maia for Internal help triage

Collect the missing context before routing the help request.

Maia asks for the fields your service teams need. A human confirms priority and ownership.

All use cases ↗

Start with the service catalog

Give Maia the current catalog, category definitions, routing rules, required intake fields, and escalation contacts. A route based on keywords alone will often fail. "Access" might concern a building, a file, a finance system, or a customer account.

Include the boundaries of the help channel. Emergencies, security reports, or sensitive people matters may require a separate path.

Ask for useful context

The intake should gather the affected service, requested outcome, impact, timing, device or environment when relevant, and steps already tried. Maia can ask targeted follow-ups instead of presenting a long generic form.

It should avoid requesting secrets, passwords, or personal details the service team does not need. If the channel audience is too broad for the issue, the response should direct the requester to the approved private route.

Propose rather than assume routing

Maia can apply the catalog rules and suggest a category and owner. Show which details led to the route. When two teams could own the issue, keep both possibilities visible and ask the service coordinator.

Priority also needs an explicit rule. A frustrated message does not by itself establish severity. The service team weighs business impact, affected people, deadlines, and safety or security criteria.

Hand the request to an owner

Post a compact intake summary in the authorized Slack channel. The receiving team confirms ownership, asks any final questions, and sets expectations. Maia can update the summary as the requester responds.

This workflow does not provision access, reset accounts, or change systems. Those actions stay with approved tools and authorized service staff.

Start with a frequent request

Choose a common, low-risk request and compare Maia's intake with what the service team normally needs. Remove questions that do not change routing, and add any required field the first run missed. Then try an ambiguous case and check that the draft asks the service coordinator instead of guessing.

Questions from internal service teams

Can Maia set ticket priority?

It can apply criteria you provide and draft a recommendation. The service owner confirms the priority.

Will it grant access?

No access action is part of this workflow. Maia collects context and prepares a route for authorized staff.

What if the request is sensitive?

Use the approved confidential channel or system. The triage reply should avoid repeating sensitive content in a shared room.

Track which intake questions actually affect routing. If requesters repeatedly supply a field that no service owner uses, remove it. If the receiving team always asks for another detail, add that requirement to the catalog.
